summary.headline: Week ahead of target on orders and revenue; the year sits exactly at target, and the pace needed for the rest of 2026 is above the recent run-rate.

points.what: Orders came in at 1,132, or 108.5% of the weekly target, and revenue at $88,836, or 120.4% of target.
points.so_what: Both target lines were beaten, so the week added to the quarter's surplus rather than drawing on it.

points.what: Revenue rose 12.3% week on week, a change the brief marks as notable, while orders rose 3.1%.
points.so_what: Revenue growth this week came from more than order volume alone, so AOV has to be read alongside orders.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is $1,929,826 against a target to date of $1,930,494, an attainment of 100.0%.
points.so_what: The ahead-of-target months of May, June and July have only brought the year level after Jan to Apr fell behind.

points.what: Revenue grew 102.0% versus the same week last year, against the 75.0% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: At this week's growth rate the business is expanding faster than the targets were built on.

points.what: Hitting the full-year target of $3,888,802 requires $85,173 of revenue a week for the remaining 23 weeks, against a current 8-week run-rate of $76,783.
points.so_what: The rest of the year needs a step up from the recent pace, so a week like this one is the requirement rather than the exception.

points.what: New signups were 232, down 3.7% on the same week last year, rated bad.
points.so_what: Signup growth is not keeping up with the order line, which is a risk to watch behind the strong revenue weeks.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 06 Jul 2026 was 10.5%, up 0.6 pp on the week before and rated bad.
points.so_what: Returns are moving in the wrong direction, which eats into the revenue reported before returns are deducted.

points.what: Revenue finished $15,042 above the weekly target and orders 89 above theirs.
points.so_what: The week closed ahead on both measures, so neither line needs to be recovered from elsewhere in the quarter.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is $316,720 against $271,853 of target, an attainment of 116.5%, with $671,276 still to go against the full-quarter target of $987,996 over 9 weeks.
points.so_what: The quarter is ahead after four weeks, but most of the quarterly target is still outstanding.

points.what: Year-to-date attainment stands at 100.0%, with $1,958,976 left against the full-year target.
points.so_what: The year has no cushion, so the quarter's surplus is what is holding the annual position level.

points.what: APAC placed 520 orders, up 5.9% week on week, contributing 29 orders or 85.3% of the total order change.
points.so_what: Almost all of the week's order growth rests on a single region.

points.what: Search delivered 784 orders, contributing 27 orders or 79.4% of the week's change.
points.so_what: The order increase is concentrated in the largest source rather than spread across channels.

points.what: Display fell 16.7% to 45 orders, a contribution of -9 orders, or -26.5% of the change.
points.so_what: Display worked against the week's order growth, so the gains elsewhere were larger than the net figure shows.

points.what: AOV was $92.06, up 6.2% week on week and outside its 8-week range, and up 3.8% on last year.
points.so_what: Baskets as well as order counts lifted revenue this week, which explains why revenue outpaced orders.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved to 14.8%, down 2.0 pp on the prior week, with each percentage point worth $1,042 of revenue.
points.so_what: Fewer cancellations kept more of the week's orders in the revenue line, supporting the 120.4% attainment.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 06 Jul 2026 was 10.5%, against 10.4% the same week last year.
points.so_what: Returns are running slightly worse than a year ago rather than improving with scale.

points.what: New signups were 232, up 0.4% week on week, while orders were up 3.1% week on week and 94.5% on last year.
points.so_what: Order growth is far outpacing signup growth, so the two lines should not be read as moving together.
